checks.detail: Ran `gh api repos/aspose-gis-foss/Aspose.GIS.FOSS-for-.Net/readme` myself: HTTP 404, exactly as facts.json claims. Also listed the repo root tree directly (`gh api .../git/trees/<sha>`): .gitignore, Aspose.GIS.FOSS.Tests, Aspose.GIS.FOSS.slnx, Aspose.GIS.FOSS -- no README file of any name, matching facts.json's F-NO-README evidence exactly.

Did NOT trust dotnet_build_log.txt as given -- performed a fresh `git clone --depth 1` of this exact repository myself into an isolated scratch directory, confirmed `git rev-parse HEAD` == b9b8c9c760bf02f6e7f06438feeabb3d0e43c1e4 (the pinned source_revision, no drift), then ran `dotnet build Aspose.GIS.FOSS.slnx -c Release` myself (dotnet 10.0.401, same SDK facts.json used). Result: exactly 381 Error(s), 45 Warning(s) -- an exact match to facts.json's claimed count and to the stored dotnet_build_log.txt. The build failure is real and independently reproduced from scratch, not merely narrated.

facts.json's evidence text states the representative missing types (Axis, GeometryType, Extent, BoundingBox, SpatialReferenceSystem, Unit, Projection, Identifier, GeographicDatum, Ellipsoid, PointsSequence, LayerIndices, LayerEvaluationRestrictions, MapInfoCoordinateValidationException/Error, WrapAttributesConverter, VectorLayer, Drivers, Dataset, GeoPackageDataset) are 'defined nowhere in the uploaded source tree.' I independently downloaded and grepped the full source tree and found this is FALSE for at least 3 of these: `BoundingBox` (public class, Common/BoundingBox.cs), `SpatialReferenceSystem` (public abstract class, SpatialReferencing/SpatialReferenceSystem.cs), and `VectorLayer` (public abstract class, Aspose.GIS.FOSS/VectorLayer.cs) all genuinely exist in the uploaded tree. Their CS0246/CS0103 errors are actually caused by missing `using` directives in the files that reference them (e.g. Geometries/Geometry.cs has `using Aspose.GIS.FOSS.SpatialReferencing;` but no `using Aspose.GIS.FOSS.Common;`; Aspose.GIS.FOSS.Tests/MainTests.cs has only `using System.Data;`, missing `using Aspose.GIS.FOSS;` entirely, which is why `VectorLayer` and the static class `Drivers` (Aspose.GIS.FOSS/Drivers.cs, which does exist) both read as undefined there). By contrast, `PointsSequence` and `GeoPackageDataset` genuinely do not exist anywhere in the tree (confirmed by grep across all 99 .cs files) -- a true missing-type defect. The 381-error build failure and the overall NON_PROCESSABLE conclusion are both still correct and independently confirmed (see C2), but the specific causal narrative in facts.json conflates two distinct defect classes (genuinely-missing source files vs. a broken/incomplete namespace-import refactor) under one 'incomplete upload' story, which overstates how much source is actually missing.

lane_r_plan.md's BLOCKED_SOURCE_INCOMPLETE conclusion (no README to anchor Lane L to; writing a Lane R README for code that does not compile would require fabricating capability claims, forbidden by mission section 7) holds independent of the C3 narrative-precision finding -- the product genuinely does not build today, for whichever precise mix of reasons, so no working example could honestly be demonstrated in either lane. Producing zero candidates is the correct, non-fabricating choice.

findings.detail: See C3. facts.json's claim that the ~15 named missing-type errors are all cases of types 'defined nowhere in the uploaded source tree' is checkably wrong for at least BoundingBox, SpatialReferenceSystem, and VectorLayer, which are genuinely present but inaccessible due to missing `using` directives in the referencing files. Only PointsSequence and GeoPackageDataset were confirmed truly absent. This does not change the bottom-line verdict (build fails with 381 real, independently-reproduced errors; NON_PROCESSABLE is correct; no fabricated README should be written) but it does mean the 'next ready action' framing in lane_r_plan.md ('missing types across ~15 files, suggesting a genuinely incomplete commit/upload') is overstated -- a meaningful fraction of the failures look more like a broken namespace-import refactor (potentially fixable with added `using` statements) mixed with a smaller number of genuinely missing source files, not uniformly 'an incomplete upload.' Worth correcting in facts.json / the upstream defect report this plan proposes as a follow-up, so that report targets the real mix of causes rather than one oversimplified story.

verdict_rationale: The core, verdict-determining claims -- no README exists, and the product does not currently build -- are both independently reproduced from scratch in this review (a live 404 from GitHub's own readme endpoint, and a fresh clone + real `dotnet build` yielding the identical 381-error outcome as the stored log), so the decision to produce NO candidate for either lane, rather than fabricate capability claims for non-compiling code, is correct and well-supported. One MODERATE finding is recorded: facts.json's root-cause narrative overgeneralizes a mix of genuinely-missing types (PointsSequence, GeoPackageDataset -- confirmed absent) and merely-inaccessible-due-to-missing-using-directive types (BoundingBox, SpatialReferenceSystem, VectorLayer -- confirmed present elsewhere in the tree) into a single 'incomplete upload' story. This affects the precision of the proposed upstream-defect-report follow-up, not the correctness of today's NON_PROCESSABLE disposition.
